purpose: Handoff from Copilot to Codex. Summarizes the full W4 SIT upload/OCR investigation chain (15-16-17) and asks for an opinion on how to proceed given a newly confirmed config/secrets-injection gap in the deploy pipeline.
requested_from_codex: Review the findings below and give an opinion on the recommended order of fixes.
Decide: delete src/config/settings.py (+ src/config/__init__.py) now, or keep it and actually wire it up later?

Decide: should docker/docker-compose.*.yml env_file loading be changed so new keys added to docker/.env.*.example actually reach an already-existing docker/.env.{stage} on the VPS, instead of only applying on first-ever file creation?
Decide: fix the sed substring-collision bug (CHANGE_ME blanket replace also matching inside sk-ant-CHANGE_ME) before or after any UAT/PROD first deploy happens.
Decide whether UAT/PROD deploy workflows need the same audit before their first real deploy (not yet verified in this pass).

two_parallel_settings_modules_exist.dead_module: src/config/settings.py (pydantic BaseSettings) — reads config/environments/{stage}.env via env_file. Only self-referenced by src/config/__init__.py. Nothing in src/backend/** imports it. Confirmed unused by grep across the repo.
two_parallel_settings_modules_exist.action_taken_this_pass: Added a header comment to src/config/settings.py documenting this finding (dated 2026-07-08, attributed to Sonnet AI review) instead of deleting it, pending team decision.

config_environments_files.status: Only consumed by the dead src/config/settings.py module. Have NO effect on real SIT/UAT/PROD runtime today. Previously used a completely different naming scheme than config/settings.py (STORAGE_ENDPOINT vs MINIO_ENDPOINT, OCR_SERVICE vs OCR_ENGINE, LLM_PROVIDER/LLM_MODEL vs STAGE_C_*/OPENROUTER_API_KEY). Already aligned to config/settings.py naming in the prior pass (commit 8a6b60e) with a clear 'not wired into live app' comment header added to each.

how_docker_env_sit_is_created: Step only runs `cp docker/.env.sit.example docker/.env.sit` + sed-based random secret generation WHEN docker/.env.sit does not already exist on the VPS (`if [ ! -f docker/.env.sit ]`).

sed replacements on first creation: CHANGE_ME_USE_openssl_rand_-hex_32 -> openssl rand -hex 32; CHANGE_ME_minimum_16_chars -> openssl rand -hex 12; CHANGE_ME_STRONG_PASSWORD -> openssl rand -hex 10; bare CHANGE_ME -> literal 'sk-ant-local-sit'.

Because docker/.env.sit already exists on the current SIT VPS (deployed previously), this whole first-creation block is skipped on every subsequent deploy run, including the deploys performed earlier in this W4 chain.
keys_refreshed_every_deploy_regardless: ADMIN_USERNAME (from optional secret SIT_APP_ADMIN_USER, default admin)
ADMIN_PASSWORD (from optional secret SIT_APP_ADMIN_PASS, default admin)
real_deploy_secret_injection_mechanics.consequence_for_todays_env_example_edits: Keys added to docker/.env.sit.example in this same session (OCR_ENGINE, DEFAULT_LOCALE, STAGE_C_PROVIDER, STAGE_C_DEFAULT_MODEL, STAGE_C_BACKUP_MODELS, STAGE_C_ESCALATION_MODEL, STAGE_C_FREE_MODELS, STAGE_C_FREE_CONF_THRESHOLD, STAGE_C_FREE_DAILY_USD_CAP, STAGE_C_PAID_DAILY_USD_CAP, STAGE_C_USE_IMAGE_INPUT) will NOT be added to the real docker/.env.sit on the current VPS by any future deploy, because the file-creation block is skipped once the file exists. They are not in the 'refreshed every deploy' list either. They will only take effect through the code-level defaults already present in config/settings.py, or if someone manually edits docker/.env.sit on the VPS, or if the deploy workflow's python `updates` dict is extended to include them.

raw_env_var_presence_via_printenv_on_con.OPENROUTER_API_KEY: present_non_empty (correctly wired every deploy from GitHub secret)
raw_env_var_presence_via_printenv_on_con.UPLOAD_ROOT: MISSING_OR_EMPTY as raw env var (resolved only via config/settings.py code default)
raw_env_var_presence_via_printenv_on_con.OCR_ENGINE: MISSING_OR_EMPTY as raw env var (resolved only via config/settings.py code default 'tesseract')

confirmed_runtime_evidence_from_diagnosi.interpretation: JWT_SECRET_KEY, MINIO_ACCESS_KEY/SECRET_KEY, and the DB password were very likely randomized once via the openssl-rand sed pass on the box's original first deploy (not left as the literal 'dev_password' / 'minioadmin' / 'dev-jwt-secret-change-me' defaults baked into config/settings.py). OPENROUTER_API_KEY is correctly refreshed every deploy from the real GitHub secret. OCR_ENGINE and other Stage C tuning keys are NOT actually set as real env vars today on the box — they only work because the current code defaults happen to already match what SIT needs (tesseract, gemini-2.5-flash, etc.). This is a coincidence, not a verified configuration, and is fragile if defaults ever change or an environment needs different tuning.

newly_found_latent_bug.bug: `sed -i "s/CHANGE_ME/sk-ant-local-sit/g" docker/.env.sit` is a blanket substring replace that also matches the `CHANGE_ME` inside `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-CHANGE_ME`, producing a garbage value `sk-ant-sk-ant-local-sit` if docker/.env.sit is ever freshly created again (e.g. new VPS, disaster recovery, or a deliberate reset).
newly_found_latent_bug.current_impact: None on the currently running SIT box (file was created before this exact template shape, or was hand-patched). Would only manifest on a future first-time file creation.
recommended_fix_options: Order the sed replacements from most-specific to least-specific pattern, or scope the bare CHANGE_ME replace to only lines matching a specific key name.
Or replace the bare-CHANGE_ME convention entirely with distinct per-key placeholder tokens (e.g. CHANGE_ME_ANTHROPIC_KEY) so no blanket substring collision is possible.

user_question_directly_answered.question: Are plaintext-looking default secrets in config/settings.py (dev_password, minioadmin, dev-jwt-secret-change-me) actually replaced by GitHub Actions secrets at deploy time, and could this be why web-upload OCR sometimes cannot be used?
user_question_directly_answered.answer_for_current_live_sit: For JWT_SECRET_KEY / MINIO_ACCESS_KEY / MINIO_SECRET_KEY / DB password: yes, real per-box random secrets were generated once via openssl rand during the box's original first deploy — confirmed present as real env vars, not the code's plaintext dev defaults. For OPENROUTER_API_KEY: yes, correctly refreshed from a real GitHub secret on every deploy. For OCR_ENGINE and the Stage C model/threshold tuning keys: no — they are not injected as real env vars at all today; the app is only working because its hardcoded code defaults happen to already be correct.
user_question_directly_answered.relationship_to_reported_ocr_failure: Diagnosis-16 reproduced a full upload -> process run on live SIT successfully (200/200, real OCR+LLM extraction). No config/secret gap was found to be the active cause of a failure in that specific run. The gaps found in this pass (17) are real but currently latent/coincidental-pass, not a confirmed active cause of the reported failure. If the user still experiences a failure, the next step is to capture the exact failing request + timestamp during a live session and correlate with backend logs (the diagnostic logging added in commit 5766800 now captures storage_provider, upload_root, ocr_engine, stage_c_provider, and openrouter_key_present on any upload/process exception).
